reason: Start with the incoming sound path by fitting the eardrum to the ear canal.
expectation: I expect an outer ear with an eardrum ready to transmit vibrations; the middle-ear connection may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The hair cells and membranes also form a sensible starting point, but I prefer to follow sound inward.

effect: The eardrum now closes the canal, so I can continue along the sound-transmitting route.
reaction: The placement is straightforward and fits what I expected.
reason: Attach the ossicles to carry eardrum vibrations into the middle ear.
expectation: I expect a connected outer- and middle-ear assembly, still needing a connection to the cochlea.

effect: The ossicles complete the sound-transmitting route up to the stapes, so the cochlea is the next part to build.
reaction: The explanation of how the small stapes footplate drives the inner ear makes the chain's purpose clearer.
reason: Fit the cochlear membranes into the fluid chambers to build the structure that will receive the vibration.
expectation: I expect a cochlear assembly with its internal membranes in place, still needing sensory cells and a nerve connection.

alternatives.reason: The sensory cells also fit the membranes, but I prefer to establish their surrounding chambers first.

effect: The cochlear membranes are in place, but their sensory-cell layer is still missing.
reaction: The cutaway makes the remaining gap clear.
reason: Add the hair cells to the cochlear membranes to build the vibration-sensing structure.
expectation: I expect hair cells positioned alongside the membranes, with an auditory nerve connection still needed.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the hair cells to nerve fibres first also seems useful, but I prefer to place them in the cochlea first.

effect: The hair cells are in place on the basilar membrane, with their nerve-contact side still exposed.
reaction: The exposed contact makes the next connection clear.
reason: Connect the auditory nerve fibres to the sensory cells; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a cochlea connected to auditory nerve fibres, though it may still need to join the sound-transmitting ear and brain.

effect: The cochlea now has a nerve connection, and the result distinguishes graded hair-cell signals from nerve action potentials.
reaction: That distinction clarifies how vibration becomes a signal.
reason: Join the mechanical route to the sensory cochlea; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the stapes to connect to the cochlear window, linking incoming vibration to the sensory structures; the assembly may still need to connect to the body and brain.

effect: The stapes now connects to the cochlea at the oval window, with the round window free to flex; the ear still needs to join the body.
reaction: The two window positions make the mechanical connection clearer.
reason: Connect the completed ear to the body and brain; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the cochlear nerve to connect into an auditory pathway toward the brain, completing the mechanical and sensory route.
